solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First part of recital: one very loud piece of music

indicators.note: the first part of the word recital is its opening letter alone

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A concert programme opens with a single thunderous number.
explanation.definitionFit: A riff is a short repeated phrase in jazz or rock, a piece of music in a loose sense.

clue.text: Think I'm home in time

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: in here says the home piece sits within the time piece

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone muses that they will be home on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home in time' reads as arriving punctually, but home is a synonym and 'in' the placing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to think up or suppose, a straightforward synonym for the verb think.

clue.text: Cornish river's ending in Penzance? Wrong

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, and with the possessive 's it gives FAL plus S

indicators.note: the ending of the word Penzance is its final letter

explanation.surface: A query whether a Cornish river really reaches the sea at Penzance, answered by Wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, the county at the south-western tip of England; Penzance is a Cornish town, but the Fal does not end there, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: False and wrong are synonyms, both meaning not correct or untrue.

clue.text: Just a minute — here are two invitations

indicators.note: two invitations means the same inviting word given twice over

parts.note: come is an invitation to approach

explanation.surface: Someone stalls, holding up a pair of invitation cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a mild remonstrance asking someone to wait or calm down, like just a minute.

clue.text: Policeman turning up clutching a hat

indicators.note: clutching means holding the other piece inside
in a down clue turning up means the letters are read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: PC is short for police constable

explanation.surface: An officer lifts his hat from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is a soft flat type of hat, so the clue defines by a general term.

clue.text: Small cake produced by the French, fine without topping

parts.note: made means produced
le is French for the

indicators.note: in a down clue the topping is the first letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A little cake baked by the French, perfectly good but lacking icing.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small shell-shaped French sponge cake, famous from Proust.

clue.text: Hurtful piece taken from newspaper

definitions.meaning: a ... remark is wounding and unkind
a press ... is an article clipped from a paper

explanation.surface: An unkind review is clipped out of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a wounding remark and a clipped press article.

clue.text: Mother runs after colleague

indicators.note: after puts the runs letter behind the colleague

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or fellow worker
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Mum jogs behind a workmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British public-school slang.

clue.text: Girl strode out, moved fast

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
loped means ran with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A young woman set off with long strides and sped along.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallop is to run at full speed, as a horse does, so the past tense means moved fast.

clue.text: Youngsters took test regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the phrase took test

explanation.surface: Some young people sat an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Tots are small children, so they are youngsters.

clue.text: Cold dessert after noon is pleasant

indicators.note: after puts the dessert behind the noon letter

parts.note: an ice is a frozen sweet

explanation.surface: An ice cream in the afternoon is agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are everyday synonyms for agreeable.

clue.text: Sheepdog seen near railway is mine

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

explanation.surface: A dog spotted by the tracks is claimed as one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as the possessive, but it is the noun: a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal pit with its buildings, an example of a mine.

clue.text: Force prisoners to exercise

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
to train is to exercise or work out

explanation.surface: Inmates are made to work out in the prison yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to compel or oblige someone, the verb force.

clue.text: Fellow stuck in cavern once

indicators.note: stuck in signals letters lodged within the words cavern once

explanation.surface: A man was once trapped inside a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernon is a man's first name, and a fellow is a man, so it is an example.

clue.text: Youngster hauled up before court case, wanting a breather

indicators.note: in a down clue hauled up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a son is a young male child

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

explanation.surface: A young man taken to court longs for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but here it is something you breathe through.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nostril is an opening in the nose for breathing, so it is whimsically a breather.

clue.text: Swallow gin cocktail, then set off

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mix, so the letters of gin are mixed
off means the letters of set are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone downs a gin drink and then leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, the verb swallow.

clue.text: Terribly hassled, subjected to cuts

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters of hassled are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A harried public service suffers budget reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashed means cut drastically, as budgets or prices are.

clue.text: Recording test case for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of test case are scattered

explanation.surface: A trial recording serves as a test case for radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a tape cartridge holding a sound recording.

clue.text: A semi-romantic bouquet

indicators.note: semi means half, so the first half of the word romantic is taken

explanation.surface: Someone sends a bunch of flowers that is only half romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like flowers, but it is a wine's scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its smell, so an aroma is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Comeback of Friends is a hit

indicators.note: a comeback runs the word backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: The return of the sitcom Friends is a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hit' looks like a success but means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a blow with the open hand, so it is a hit.

clue.text: Son with desire to be chic

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A boy longs to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British slang for smart and fashionable, like chic.

clue.text: For example, Othello encore on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a call of encore is a call for more

explanation.surface: A broadcast of Shakespeare's tragedy draws calls for a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, so he is an example of a Moor.

clue.text: A mixed grill, hot, short of nothing, OK?

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of grill are jumbled
short of means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner checks the hot mixed grill came up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of nothing' removes O from HOT, leaving HT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means satisfactory or acceptable, the same as OK.

clue.text: Some believe made-up story

indicators.note: some means only a part of the word believe is taken

explanation.surface: Some people believe an invented tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is a falsehood, a story invented to deceive.

clue.text: Standard weapon, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a lance is a long spear used by knights

explanation.surface: A regulation weapon, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking or idiom, as in legal parlance.

clue.text: Conceal Jekyll's alter ego, you say?

indicators.note: you say means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's evil other self in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: Hide the dark self of Dr Jekyll, as the phrase goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight, a synonym.
